about: Two proposed, untested device types entered as open device nodes by push/c18-repair-owed-record-r17-open-device-nodes (campaign round 18) so that generate.py can rank explore slots. Not leads: no lane has passed stage A on either. Entry conditions and the controls that must fail are in curated/devices.json (fields entryConditions, controlsThatMustFail). Tags are the reader's: each geometric-program tag is one that the round-18 planner named as a carrier for the type. Round 19 (push/c19-repair-owed-record-r18-checkpoint-prep): both types are closed in curated/devices.json on the referee files of their round-18 lanes (one referee per lane); names and statements below say what those files hold. Tags, type and status fields are unchanged.

nodes.name: Closed device type (round 18, one referee per lane): one-sided completion bound in the band 1/2 < theta <= 1
nodes.statement: Proposed, untested device type. Question: is there a one-sided bound N(theta) for the band operator T_Z (the Weil form on tests supported on an interval of length u = theta log(t/2 pi)), 1/2 < theta <= 1, with a completion term taken from the reflected half of the approximate functional equation or from the pole term, that zeta satisfies and every control fails at a named step. Background (window information law, one referee): band devices are forms of one operator; between P = sqrt(t/2 pi) and P = t/2 pi the missing input is this bound; the truncated Euler product identity holds for every completely multiplicative chain and is not that input; sign chains fail the bound at theta >= 1 only in measurements. Carriers named by the planner: bridge and antibridge Hankel blocks, pole-term Schur complement. No inequality is on file. Not a statement about zeros. Outcome, round 18 (map row P58; one referee per lane): closed. N(theta) below the Nyquist band is, by an exact truncation identity valid for every Dirichlet series with a_1 = 1, a statement about the zeros of the partial sum D_P; no step uses multiplicativity; the reflected half is not seen by the band; ZQ passes for theta' < 1 in the lattice model; at theta' = 1 the statement is the target in a window. Measured on 96 modes at heights 1e6 to 1e12: the linear reflected completion is not a positive extension (zeta fails it in 600 of 600 cells); ZQ, E_0.1, DH and multiplicative sign chains pass N(theta) in parts of the band, with a dependence on the number of modes.
nodes.source: push/c17-window-information-law-ctheta-u5/RESULT.md section 3 and REFEREE.md; campaign/ROUND_LOG.md round 17 (lesson 5, combinable 2) and round 18 allocation (lanes 2, 3); entered by push/c18-repair-owed-record-r17-open-device-nodes; outcome entered by push/c19-repair-owed-record-r18-checkpoint-prep from push/c18-tz-one-sided-bound-fe-reserve-bridge, push/c18-tz-band-completion-controls-server, push/c18-exact-relation-rigidity-klein-spinor (REFEREE.md each)

nodes.name: Closed device type (round 18, one referee): exact-relation rigidity
nodes.statement: Proposed, untested device type. Question: is there an exact relation that zeta satisfies at defect 0, on a class that excludes the symmetric-factor twins by the support clause and the non-rational local factor by integrality, whose failure set is open in a topology in which the zero set moves continuously, and which a named control fails for a multiplicative reason. Background (round 17, one referee each): positivity of a state is invariant under conjugation by an invertible element, so twins of the form b xi are rejected only by an exact relation; a quantitative identification is target-level; stability reads the functional equation and integrality. Carriers named by the planner: Klein seam identity, spinor square root S causal, Bost-Connes twin ladder. No relation is on file. Not a statement about zeros. Outcome, round 18 (map row X1; one referee): closed. Ordinary multiplicativity replaces no clause of the identifications on file: control HQ2 = zeta(s)(1 + eps u^2/(1 - u)^4), u = q^(1/2 - s), has the exact functional equation, integer frequencies, multiplicative coefficients >= 1 and zeros off the line, with a pole of order 4 at 1/2; TN1 = zeta(s)(1 + q^(3/4 - s)) lacks only the functional equation. The clause that completes the identification is analyticity on the critical line. Of the relations listed only the definition a(pn) = a(n) and the target J = 1 exclude every control.
